patch.value: Single source of surface tiering: one contract-declared tier per command drives CLI help, MCP tool profiles, completions, and docs together

Four separate efforts each decide, independently, which part of pm's surface an agent sees first: tiered CLI help, MCP tool profiles capping the exposed tool count, hiding completion helper entrypoints, and hiding the internal test-runs worker. Each is correct on its own and all four answer the same question — what tier is this command in — with four mechanisms that will drift apart the moment one is edited without the others. Declare the tier once, as a field on the command contract, and derive all four surfaces from it. The tiers themselves are the decision: a core tier an agent must know to work, a standard tier it reaches for by name, a full tier that exists and is documented, and an internal tier that is reachable but never advertised. Deriving everything from one field also makes the one-screen claim testable rather than aspirational, because the core tier's rendered size is a number the gate can check.

Every command declares exactly one tier in contract data, and help, MCP tool profiles, shell completions, and generated docs derive visibility from that field alone; A test asserts no surface maintains its own independent visibility list; The core tier's rendered help size is asserted against the one-screen budget, making the claim mechanically checked; The first landing changes no visible surface, proven by before-and-after snapshots of help, tool lists, and completions; Changing a command's tier is a single-field change whose effect on all four surfaces appears in one regenerated snapshot diff; Package-contributed commands declare a tier through the same field, so extensions cannot bypass tiering
Surface visibility is one declared property, not four independently maintained lists
Four mechanisms answering one question is a drift generator; drift here means an agent sees different surfaces through CLI and MCP and cannot trust either
Consolidates four visibility mechanisms into one contract field; the visible surfaces should be unchanged on the first landing, proven by snapshots
Raising or lowering a command's visibility is a one-field change that updates help, MCP tools, completions, and docs at once

message: File the tiering consolidation that keeps four visibility mechanisms from drifting apart
